In the context of quaternary cytoreductive surgery (QRS) in ovarian cancer, it appears that the surgical effort is not a determining factor for survival in patients with advanced disease. While maximal therapeutic effort combining optimal surgery and chemotherapy has been shown to significantly prolong survival in selected patients, even in highly advanced settings such as the third Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) relapse.

This suggests that, while surgical expertise is crucial in achieving optimal results, it is not a sole determinant of outcome. Instead, the overall effectiveness of the treatment approach, including chemotherapy and surgery, plays a more significant role in determining patient survival.

In other words, the quality of care provided during QRS is more important than the quantity of surgical effort. Patients with advanced ovarian cancer often face complex and challenging conditions, and their outcomes are influenced by various factors beyond just the number of surgeries performed.
